recipes.title: Cheesy Mexican-Spiced Grilled Gnocchi
method: Grate carrot. Thinly slice spring onion. Roughly chop capsicum. Drain sweetcorn.
In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over high heat. Cook capsicum, corn and carrot, tossing, until lightly browned, 4-6 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
Wipe out frying pan, then return to medium-high heat with a generous drizzle of olive oil. When oil is hot, cook gnocchi, tossing occasionally, until golden, 6-8 minutes.

Preheat grill to medium-high. To pan with the gnocchi, add Mexican Fiesta spice blend and garlic paste. Cook, tossing, until fragrant, 1 minute. Return cooked veggies to the pan, then add the water, the brown sugar, the butter and passata. Stir to combine, then simmer until slightly thickened, 1-2 minutes. Season to taste.
Transfer the saucy gnocchi to a baking dish. Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese. Grill until cheese is melted and golden, 5-10 minutes.
Divide cheesy Mexican-spiced grilled gnocchi between bowls. Top with chilli flakes (if using) and sprinkle over spring onions to serve.

recipes.title: Herby Steak & Chimichurri Sauce with Flatbread
method: Place beef between two sheets of baking paper. Pound beef with a meat mallet or rolling pin until slightly flattened. Season beef. In a large frying pan, heat olive oil over high heat. Cook beef, turning, for 3-6 minutes (depending on thickness), or until cooked to your liking. In the last min, sprinkle with seasoning, turn to coat. Transfer to a plate to rest.
Roughly chop tomato and apple. In a bowl, combine tomato, apple, chargrilled capsicums, salad leaves and dressing. Toss and season.
Toast or grill flatbreads to your liking. Slice steak. Plate up steak and salad. Sprinkle with almonds and spoon over chimichurri. Serve with flatbread.

recipes.title: Aussie Pork & Rainbow Veggie Toss
method: Preheat oven to 240°C/220°C fan-forced. Thinly slice carrot into rounds. Cut brown onion and tomato into thick wedges. Cut beetroot into small chunks. Roughly tear kale leaves, then discard the stems. Set kale aside. Place carrot, onion, tomato and beetroot on a lined oven tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat. Roast until almost tender, 15-18 minutes. Remove veggies from oven. Add kale and a pinch of salt to the tray. Gently toss to combine. Return to oven to roast until tender, a further 5-8 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely chop garlic. In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil and garlic over medium-high heat. Cook until fragrant, 1 minute. Transfer to a small bowl.
Add Greek-style yoghurt to garlic oil mixture. Stir to combine, then season to taste. Set aside.

In a medium bowl, combine Aussie spice blend and a drizzle of olive oil. Add pork loin steaks, turning to coat. Return frying pan to medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. When oil is hot, cook pork until cooked through, 3-4 minutes each side (depending on thickness). Set aside on a plate and cover with foil to rest for 5 minutes.
Add a drizzle of white wine vinegar to the roast veggie tray. Gently toss to combine. Season to taste.
Slice Aussie-spiced pork. Divide roast veggie toss between plates. Top with pork (plus any resting juices!). Spoon garlic yoghurt over pork. Sprinkle with pine nuts to serve.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Zesty Beef & Broccoli
buy: 1 tub Fish Sauce & Rice Vinegar Mix
method: In a medium saucepan, bring the water (for the rice) to the boil. Add the jasmine rice, stir, cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 12 minutes, then remove the pan from the heat and keep covered until the rice is tender and all the water is absorbed, 10-15 minutes.

While the rice is cooking, zest the lime, then cut into wedges. Combine the oyster sauce, sweet chilli sauce, fish sauce & rice vinegar mix, brown sugar and lime zest in a medium bowl. Add the beef strips and toss to coat. Set aside.

Chop the broccoli into small florets and roughly chop the stalk. Finely chop the garlic. Thinly slice the red onion. Thinly slice the long red chilli (if using). Pick and roughly tear the mint leaves.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the broccoli and a splash of water and cook until tender, 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, 1 minute. Transfer to a bowl and cover to keep warm.

Return the frying pan to a high heat with a drizzle more olive oil. Add the onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes. Add the beef strips and cook, tossing, until browned, 1-2 minutes. Add the water and cook until just bubbling. Remove from the heat and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Divide the jasmine rice between plates and top with the Vietnamese beef and broccoli. Garnish with the long red chilli (if using) and mint leaves. Serve with the lime wedges.

recipes.title: Sweet Chilli Pork Burger
method: Preheat the oven to 240°C/220°C fan-forced. Slice the potato (unpeeled) into 1cm fries. Place on an oven tray lined with baking paper. Season with salt, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Toss to coat, then spread out in a single layer and bake until tender, 20-25 minutes.

While the fries are baking, finely chop the coriander and garlic. Grate the ginger. Cut the cucumber into rounds. In a small bowl, combine a splash of water, sweet chilli sauce and 2 tsp soy sauce (for the glaze). Set aside.
In a medium bowl, place 1/2 the garlic aioli. Add the slaw mix and coriander. Season with salt and pepper.

In a large bowl, combine the pork mince, garlic, fine breadcrumbs, 1 tbs soy sauce (for the patties), ginger, egg and season with pepper. Using damp hands, shape the pork mixture into evenly sized patties, slightly larger than your burger buns. In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over a medium-high heat. Cook the pork patties until cooked through, 5-6 minutes each side. When the patties are cooked, add the sweet chilli glaze to the pan and then remove the pan from the heat. Flip the patties to coat.
While the patties are cooking, place the bake-athome burger buns on a wire rack in the oven until heated through, 2-3 minutes.

Toss the slaw. Cut the burger buns in half. Spread the remaining garlic aioli over the base of the buns and top with pork patties, any sweet chilli glaze remaining in the pan and some of the cucumber and slaw. Serve the sesame fries and any remaining cucumber and slaw on the side.

recipes.title: Spiced Beef & Hummus Tacos
method: Thinly slice the red onion. Finely chop the garlic. Finely chop the tomato and cucumber. Roughly chop the parsley. Mix the hummus with 1 tbs water (for the hummus).

In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over a high heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, 1 minute. Add the beef mince and cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned, 3-4 minutes.
While the beef is cooking, add the cucumber, tomato and parsley to a medium bowl. Add the white wine vinegar, a drizzle of olive oil and season with salt and pepper.

Add the chermoula spice blend, tomato paste, beef stock pot and brown sugar to the beef. Cook, stirring, until fragrant, 1-2 minutes. Add the butter and 1/4 cup water (for the beef) and simmer until the sauce has thickened, 1-2 minutes. Season to taste.
Heat the mini flour tortillas on a plate in the microwave for 10 second bursts, until warmed through.
Toss the salsa to coat. Bring everything to the table to serve. Build your tacos by filling each tortilla with mixed salad leaves, Turkish spiced beef and cucumber salsa. Drizzle with the hummus.

recipes.title: Japanese Beef Bowl
method: In a medium saucepan, bring 1.25 cups water (for the rice) to the boil. Add the jasmine rice, stir, cover with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 12 minutes, then remove the pan from the heat and keep covered until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed, 10-15 minutes.

While the rice is cooking, thinly slice the red onion. In a small bowl, combine the vinegar, 1/4 cup water (for the onion) and a generous pinch of sugar and salt. Scrunch the onion in your hands, then add to the pickling liquid and stir to coat. Set aside until serving.

Finely grate the ginger. Finely grate the garlic. In a medium bowl, combine the ginger, garlic, soy sauce and honey. Add the beef strips and toss to coat. Set aside. Thinly slice the carrot (unpeeled) into half-moons. Chop the capsicum into 2cm pieces. Roughly chop the Asian greens.

Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the mixed sesame seeds and toast, tossing, until golden, 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a medium bowl. Return the frying pan to a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the carrot and capsicum and cook until tender, 4-5 minutes. Add the Asian greens and cook until tender, 1 minute. Transfer to the bowl with the sesame seeds, along with the Japanese dressing. Toss to coat.
Return the frying pan to a high heat along with a drizzle of olive oil. Shaking off any excess marinade, cook the beef strips in batches, tossing, until browned, 1-2 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Drain the pickled onion. Divide the rice between bowls. Top with the sesame veggies, Japanese beef and pickled onion. Serve with the coconut sweet chilli mayonnaise.

recipes.title: Greek-Style Lamb Gyros & Garlicky Fries
method: Preheat oven to 240°C/220°C fan-forced. To a baking dish, add slow-cooked lamb shoulder, including any packet juices. Sprinkle with dried oregano and a good pinch of salt. Cover with foil, then roast for 25 minutes. Remove from oven. Uncover, then turn over lamb. Roast, uncovered, until browned and heated through, 10-12 minutes. Set aside to rest, covered, for 5 minutes. Shred lamb using two forks.

While lamb is roasting, thinly slice onion. In a small bowl, combine the red wine vinegar and a good pinch of sugar and salt. Scrunch sliced onion in your hands, then add to pickling liquid. Add enough water to just cover onion. Set aside.

Cut potato into fries. Place on a lined oven tray. Sprinkle over garlic & herb seasoning, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and toss to coat. Spread out in a single layer. Bake until tender, 20-25 minutes.

Finely chop garlic. Roughly chop tomato, kalamata olives and dill. Thinly slice cucumber. Cut lemon into wedges. In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil and the garlic over medium-high heat. Cook until fragrant, 1 minute. Transfer to a small bowl. Add Greek-style yoghurt, dill and fetta cubes to garlic oil mixture. Stir to combine.

Drizzle (or brush) each flatbread with olive oil. Return frying pan to medium-high heat. Cook flatbreads until golden and warmed through, 1-2 minutes each side. Meanwhile, combine mixed salad leaves, cucumber, tomato and olives in a large bowl. Add a drizzle of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice. Toss to combine. Season to taste.

Drain pickled onion. Bring everything to the table to serve. Top flatbreads with a helping of salad, Greek-style lamb, garlicky fries and pickled onion. Spoon over the dill yoghurt-fetta sauce. Tear over the mint. Serve with any remaining fries, salad and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Marinated Salt & Pepper Barramundi with Green Beans, Soy-Ginger Sauce & Rice
method: Add the water to a medium saucepan and bring to the boil. Add jasmine rice and a pinch of salt. Stir, cover with a lid and reduce heat to low. Cook for 12 minutes, then remove pan from heat. Keep covered until rice is tender and the water is absorbed, 10-15 minutes. Stir the butter through the rice.

While rice is cooking, trim green beans and cut into thirds. Cut barramundi into 2cm chunks. Crush black peppercorns with a pestle and mortar, or in their sachet with a rolling pin. In a medium bowl, combine cornflour, crushed peppercorns and the salt. Add barramundi, tossing to coat. In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, honey and ginger paste.
In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium-high heat. Cook green beans, tossing regularly, until tender, 4-5 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.

Return frying pan to high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. When oil is hot, shake excess flour off barramundi, then cook barramundi, turning occasionally, until golden and just cooked through, 4-6 minutes.
Return green beans to pan. Add soy-ginger mixture and cook, tossing to coat, until heated through, 30 seconds.
Divide rice between bowls. Top with salt and pepper barramundi and green beans, spooning over any remaining soy-ginger sauce from the pan. Tear over herbs to serve.

recipes.title: Quick Japanese-Style Beef Tacos
method: Finely chop garlic and celery. Thinly slice onion. In a small bowl, combine garlic, ginger paste, the soy sauce and honey.

In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium-high heat. Cook onion until tender, 4-5 minutes. Transfer to a bowl. Return pan to high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. When oil is hot, cook beef strips, in batches (to help it stay tender), until browned and cooked through, 1-2 minutes. Return beef strips and onion to pan. Add honey-soy mixture and simmer until heated through, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat.

While ingredients are simmering, combine Japanese dressing and a drizzle of olive oil in a medium bowl. Add slaw mix, celery and 1/2 the mixed sesame seeds. Toss to coat. Set aside. Microwave mini flour tortillas on a plate in 10 second bursts, until heated through.
Spread each tortilla with garlic aioli. Fill with a helping of slaw, Japanese-style beef and cucumber. Sprinkle with remaining sesame seeds to serve.

recipes.title: Katsu-Glazed Tofu Tacos & Aioli Slaw
method: Finely chop garlic. Cut Japanese tofu into 1cm cubes. Grate carrot. Thinly slice pear. In a medium bowl, combine shredded cabbage mix and garlic aioli. Season to taste. Set aside.
In a small bowl, combine garlic, the honey, katsu paste, mixed sesame seeds and a dash of water. Set aside.

In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium-high heat. Cook tofu, turning often, until browned, 2-4 minutes. Add katsu mixture and cook, turning tofu to coat, until slightly sticky, 1-2 minutes. Microwave mini flour tortillas on a plate in 10 second bursts, until warmed through.
Finely slice long chilli (if using). Fill tortillas with creamy slaw, pear, carrot and katsu glazed tofu. Sprinkle with chilli and crispy shallots to serve.

recipes.title: Seared Beef Rump & Roast Veggie Toss
method: Preheat oven to 240°C/220°C fan-forced. Thickly slice carrot into half-moons. Cut sweet potato into bite-sized chunks. Cut beetroot into 1cm chunks.

Place prepped veggies on a lined oven tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast until tender, 20-25 minutes. When the veggies have 8 minutes remaining, add baby spinach and a pinch of salt to the tray. Gently toss to combine. Roast until tender, a further 5-8 minutes.
Place beef rump between two sheets of baking paper. Pound beef with a meat mallet or rolling pin until slightly flattened. Season beef with salt and pepper.

In a large frying pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over high heat. When oil is hot, cook the beef, turning, for 3-6 minutes (depending on thickness), or until cooked to your liking. Transfer to a plate to rest.
While the steak is resting, add the white wine vinegar to the roast veggie tray. Gently toss to combine.
Slice the seared steak. Divide steak and roast veggie toss between plates. Spoon any resting juices over steak. Top with a dollop of mustard mayo to serve.

recipes.title: Smoky Pork Loaded Wedges
method: Preheat oven to 220°C. Line 2 large oven trays with baking paper. Cut unpeeled potatoes into wedges, drizzle with 2 tbsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast, swapping trays halfway, for about 30 minutes or until tender.

Cut capsicums into 1cm chunks. Thinly slice spring onion, including the green part. Crush or finely chop garlic. Drain and rinse beans. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large deep frypan over high heat; cook pork mince, breaking up lumps, for 3–4 minutes until browned. Remove from pan, leaving any oil behind.

Return pan to medium heat. Cook capsicum and garlic for about 5 minutes until softened. Add pork, beans, smoky barbecue seasoning, barbecue sauce and water. Bring to the boil and simmer for about 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Season to taste.
Transfer potato wedges to one oven tray. Spoon pork mixture over the wedges and bake for about 5 minutes or until warmed through.
Mix mayonnaise with 1 tbsp water; season with salt and pepper. Divide loaded wedges among bowls, drizzle with mayo sauce and scatter over spring onion.
Feed-a-crowd note from source: if mayonnaise is unavailable, use plain yoghurt instead.

recipes.title: Family Fave Lamb Meatballs with Peas, Penne & Pesto
method: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil for the pasta. Coarsely grate zucchini and carrots. Crush or finely chop garlic.
Combine lamb mince, half the mint and rosemary seasoning and 2 tsp cornflour in a bowl. Season generously with salt and pepper and shape into walnut-sized meatballs.
Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a large deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook meatballs, turning regularly, for 3–4 minutes until browned but not cooked through. Remove from pan.

Cook zucchini, carrot and garlic in the same pan for 2–3 minutes until starting to soften. Stir in diced tomatoes, remaining mint and rosemary seasoning, water and sugar. Bring to a simmer; reduce heat, cover and cook about 10 minutes.
While the sauce cooks, boil penne for about 7–8 minutes. Add peas, return to the boil and cook for another minute, until pasta is al dente. Drain.
Add meatballs to the sauce, cover and cook 2–3 minutes until cooked through. Add pasta and peas and gently combine. Divide among bowls and drizzle with basil pesto.

recipes.title: Healthy Korean Beef Wrap with Crunchy Salad
method: Peel and grate ginger and thinly slice onion. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook beef mince, ginger and onion for 3–4 minutes, breaking up lumps, until browned and onion has softened. Season with salt and pepper, add Korean sauce and simmer until thickened.
Peel and grate carrot. Trim sugar snap peas and slice into thin strips. Thinly slice red radishes and spring onion. Combine the crunchy vegetables with mayonnaise, salt and pepper.
Prepare the garnish/sauce as directed on the source card using the supplied soy sauce, mayonnaise and sesame seeds. Warm pita bread just before serving.
Spread sauce over warm pita, then arrange mesclun, Korean beef and crunchy salad. Finish with sesame seeds and serve.

recipes.title: Veggie-Loaded Pork Stir-Fry
method: Rinse short grain rice and place in a medium pot with 3 cups water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, cover, reduce heat and cook 15–20 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and rest covered.
Peel and cut carrots into half-moons. Deseed and dice capsicums. Slice mushrooms. Halve zucchini lengthways and thinly slice.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Cook carrot, capsicum, mushrooms and pork mince, breaking up lumps, for about 6–8 minutes until the mince is browned. Season with salt and pepper.
Whisk mushroom broth with arrowroot mix until smooth. Chop spring onion and add to the sauce mixture.
Add zucchini and the mushroom-broth mixture to the pan. Stir-fry until zucchini is tender and sauce has thickened. Remove from heat and check seasoning.
Fluff rice and divide among plates. Top with pork and vegetable stir-fry and sprinkle with sesame-shallot mix.

recipes.title: Fast Family Fave Tex-Mex Beef with Black Beans, Rice & Avocado
method: Cook basmati rice in boiling water for about 12 minutes or until tender. Drain and keep covered and warm.
Thinly slice capsicums, discarding seeds. Coarsely chop tomatoes. Crush or finely chop garlic. Rinse and drain black beans.
Toss beef stir-fry with Tex-Mex seasoning and garlic. Heat a generous drizzle of olive oil in a large frypan over high heat and cook beef in batches for 1–2 minutes until browned. Remove from pan.
Reduce heat to medium-high. Cook capsicum in olive oil for about 3 minutes. Add tomato, black beans, tomato paste and 250ml (1 cup) water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook about 3 minutes.

Return beef and resting juices to the vegetable mixture. Remove from heat; stir in red wine vinegar and sugar and season with salt and pepper. Divide rice and beef mixture among bowls, top with avocado and drizzle with extra virgin olive oil if desired.

recipes.title: Thai Beef Noodle Salad with Mint, Lime & Peanuts
buy: mint leaves (quantity not stated on scan)
method: Crush or finely chop garlic. Combine garlic, Thai seasoning and oil in a large bowl; season with salt and pepper. Add beef stir-fry and toss to coat.

method: Thinly slice onion. Quarter carrots lengthways, then thinly slice. Trim fennel and thinly slice. Crumble stock cubes into a heatproof jug, add tomato paste and boiling water and stir to dissolve.

Add pork mince to the vegetables and cook, breaking up lumps, for 3–4 minutes until browned.
Add stock mixture to the pork and vegetables and bring to the boil. Reduce heat to medium and simmer 12–15 minutes until sauce has reduced. Season with salt and pepper.
Finely grate parmesan. Whisk extra virgin olive oil and balsamic vinegar in a large bowl with salt and pepper.

Boil gnocchi for about 3 minutes, or until cooked, then drain. Add gnocchi to the sauce and combine. Toss salad leaves with dressing. Divide gnocchi among bowls, scatter with parmesan and serve with dressed leaves.

method: Pick coriander leaves and finely chop stems. Crush or finely chop garlic. Thinly slice spring onions and chilli. Crumble stock cubes into a heatproof jug, add boiling water and stir to dissolve.

Pat fish dry and grate ginger. Fry fish over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes each side or until cooked. Add ginger and teriyaki sauce and glaze the fish; warm bok choi in the pan.
Add cooked noodles to the vegetable bowl. Add peanut dressing and crispy shallots and toss well.

method: Preheat oven to 240°C (220°C fan). Peel and cut sweet potato into wedges. Arrange on a lined oven tray, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and bake 20–25 minutes or until tender.
Place flour on a plate. Break eggs into a small bowl and whisk. Zest lemon into another bowl, add breadcrumbs and a drizzle of olive oil, combine and season.
Pat fish fillets dry and cut into large bite-sized pieces. Season, dust in flour, dip in egg and coat in breadcrumbs. Place on a second lined oven tray and bake 15–20 minutes, turning halfway.
Thinly slice apple. Combine apple, coleslaw, dressing base and yoghurt in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper and mix well.

pantry: 1/2 cup rice wine vinegar or white vinegar
method: Finely mince lemongrass, garlic and shallot. Combine with fish sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar and oil. Add pork belly strips and toss to coat. Marinate for 20 minutes (up to 2 hours for more flavour).
Place carrot and daikon in a bowl. Stir vinegar, sugar, salt and water until dissolved, pour over vegetables and stand at least 20 minutes. Drain well before using.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook pork in a single layer, in batches if needed, for 3–4 minutes per side until golden, caramelised and cooked through.
Warm rolls at 180°C for about 3 minutes until crisp. Slice open and spread pâté on one side and Kewpie mayonnaise on the other.
Layer caramelised pork into rolls and top with drained pickles, cucumber, fresh coriander and sliced chilli.
Drizzle with Maggi Liquid Seasoning to taste, close the rolls and serve immediately while hot and crisp.

recipes.title: Egg-Free Chicken Katsu
pantry: salt and black pepper to taste
method: Whisk ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, sugar, garlic powder and onion powder until smooth; set aside.
Set up three shallow bowls: flour, cornstarch slurry made with water, and panko breadcrumbs. Stir slurry again just before using.
Pound chicken to about 1/2-inch thickness. Season with salt and pepper, coat in flour, dip in slurry and press firmly into panko.
Heat about 1.5 inches of oil in a heavy pan to 170°C / 340°F over medium heat.
Fry chicken for 3–4 minutes per side until deeply golden, crisp and cooked through, working in batches so the pan is not crowded.
Drain on a wire rack or paper towel-lined plate, rest 2 minutes, slice into 1-inch strips and drizzle with katsu sauce.

method: Whisk rice flour, cornflour, turmeric and salt. Gradually whisk in water and coconut milk until smooth. Stir in spring onion if using and rest batter about 30 minutes (up to 2 hours).
Season pork and prawns lightly. Keep bean sprouts and sliced onion ready.
Heat a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Add 1 tsp oil, fry a few pork slices 1–2 minutes, add prawns and onion and cook until prawns begin turning opaque.
Stir batter. Pour in about 80ml, immediately swirling into a very thin layer. Scatter over bean sprouts. Cover and cook 1–2 minutes.
Uncover, drizzle a little oil around the edge and cook 3–5 minutes until deeply crisp underneath. Fold in half and serve immediately with lettuce, herbs and nuoc cham.

1 cup packed mint, Thai basil and coriander
method: Soak sliced onion in iced water for about 10 minutes to soften its bite and make it crisp. Drain thoroughly and pat dry.
Place pork in gently simmering salted water and cook until the centre reaches 63°C; rest 3 minutes. Cool and slice thinly.
Poach raw prawns in the pork cooking liquid for 2–3 minutes until opaque and firm. Drain, cool and halve lengthways.
Stir warm water and sugar until dissolved. Add fish sauce, lime, garlic and chilli; taste for a bold sweet-sour-salty balance.
Combine mango, carrot, onion, pork, prawns and herbs. Add dressing just before serving and toss gently. Finish with peanuts and fried shallots.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Chả Giò - Crisp Fried Spring Rolls
buy: 25g dried wood-ear mushrooms, soaked, drained and chopped
50g glass noodles, soaked, drained and cut
method: Mix all filling ingredients thoroughly until evenly combined. Refrigerate about 15 minutes. Fry a teaspoonful and taste to check seasoning before rolling.

Place 1 heaped tablespoon filling near the lower third. Fold in sides and roll firmly without squeezing so tightly that the wrapper splits. Keep rolls covered with a damp towel.

recipes.title: Marinated Thai Beef Salad
method: Whisk fish sauce, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, garlic, oil and black pepper until sugar dissolves. Add beef, coat well and refrigerate at least 1 hour (up to 24 hours). Bring to room temperature about 30 minutes before cooking.

Remove beef from marinade and pat dry. Sear in a smoking-hot skillet for about 2 minutes each side for medium-rare (or about 2.5 minutes each side for medium).
Rest beef loosely tented with foil for 10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Toss mixed lettuce with a little dressing. Combine sliced beef with cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, coriander and mint. Dress with most remaining dressing and toss gently.
Pile dressed lettuce onto plates, top with beef and salad, sprinkle with peanuts and extra herbs, drizzle remaining dressing and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Sardine & Shallot Pasta
buy: 2 x 120g tinned sardines in oil, drained
1/4 cup packed fresh parsley leaves, chopped
1/4 cup loose fresh dill fronds, chopped
method: Put a large pot of water on to boil for pasta. Gather ingredients; slice shallots, chop herbs and drain sardines.
Heat olive oil in a wide heavy-based pan over medium-low heat. Add shallots and a pinch of salt; cook slowly for about 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very soft and sweet.
Toast pine nuts in a small saucepan over low heat until golden, watching closely. Remove immediately to a bowl.
Cook spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve about 1/2 cup pasta water before draining.

Add sardines to the shallots and stir, breaking up larger chunks. Add juice of one lemon, drained pasta and a small splash of pasta water. Turn heat up slightly and stir until combined, adding more pasta water if needed.
Off heat, drizzle with white wine vinegar and stir. Taste and add more lemon if desired. Top with toasted pine nuts and chopped herbs and serve with leftover lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Easy Pumpkin Pasta
pantry: extra virgin olive oil, generous drizzle
method: Preheat oven to 180°C. Place pumpkin on a baking tray with garlic and onion halves, keeping garlic/onion near the middle so they do not burn. Drizzle generously with olive oil and season.
Roast about 15–20 minutes, turn everything and remove any garlic that is already golden. Roast a further 15–20 minutes until pumpkin is golden and tender and onion has softened.
Squeeze roasted garlic from skins into a food processor with pumpkin and onion. Add crème fraîche and cracked black pepper and blitz until smooth; taste and season.
Heat butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add sage leaves and a sprinkle of salt; cook until crisp. Remove sage to paper towel and pour browned butter into a bowl.
Cook fresh pasta until al dente, reserving about 1/2 cup pasta water. Drain and return to the pot. Pour over pumpkin sauce, add a splash of pasta water if needed and combine.
Serve hot, topped with crispy sage, browned butter and parmesan if desired.

recipes.title: Quick Ravioli with Mint Yoghurt
method: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Add ravioli and cook according to packet directions until al dente. Drain; rinse under cool running water if serving at room temperature.
Combine yoghurt, garlic and salt with black pepper. Stir in mint and olive oil, then thin with water to pouring consistency.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and add pine nuts. Cook until brown milk solids appear, butter smells nutty and pine nuts are golden; immediately pour into a heatproof bowl.
Toss ravioli with yoghurt dressing and season. Spoon over brown butter and pine nuts, scatter with smoked paprika and a few mint leaves, and squeeze over lemon.

recipes.title: Pasta e Fagioli
method: Warm olive oil in a large pot over low-medium heat. Add shallots, celery and carrot with a pinch of salt and sweat very gently for about 10 minutes until soft and just colouring.
Add garlic, rosemary and chilli flakes if using and cook a few minutes until fragrant. Stir in beans and passata.
Increase heat to high and add stock. Drop in parmesan rind if using. Bring to the boil, reduce to a simmer and cook about 10 minutes.
Remove about half the soup, avoiding the rind, and blitz until smooth. Return it to the pot to give the soup body; add extra stock if too thick.
Add pasta, keep soup simmering gently and cook until pasta is al dente and soup is thick, about 10 minutes depending on pasta shape. Add stock or water if needed.
Discard parmesan rind and season to taste. Ladle into bowls, drizzle with olive oil, scatter with grated parmesan and add chilli flakes if desired.

recipes.title: Pork & Fennel Sausage Pasta
buy: 2 small fennel bulbs + stalks, finely sliced
method: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil. Add casarecce and cook to packet directions.
Heat olive oil in a large frying pan. Add sausage mince and break into crumbly bits. Once browned, add garlic and deglaze with white wine.
Remove browned mince and reserve. Add fennel and radicchio to the pan, increase heat and cook until softened.
Reserve a mugful of pasta cooking water, then drain pasta.
Return mince and pasta to the vegetables. Add half the parmesan and enough pasta water to loosen; stir until sauce reduces and thickens.
Divide among bowls and top with remaining parmesan, reserved fennel fronds, cracked pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.
recipes.allergens: Contains gluten (pasta), milk (cheese) and sulphites (wine). Sausages may contain other allergens; check current product labels.
